title: Curated rollout + quiet launch notes: Autobatch Advisor
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick personal scratch for the small-batch, quiet rollout of Autobatch Advisor (first internal pilot).
- Primary goal: validate safety and perf signals in production with minimal user impact. Not a public launch.
- Secondary: exercise canary => SRE/Support runbook and get monitoring dashboards stable.

Goals for the pilot (what success looks like):
- No customer-facing errors attributable to advisor in the first 72 hours.
- Latency delta within +8ms p50 and +25ms p95 vs baseline for canary traffic.
- Advisor decisions result in >=10% token-cost reduction for targeted workloads (mini cohort) or show clear path to improvement.
- Observability: dashboards green, traces annotated, and the KV cache hit metric tracked per model.

Quick timeline (target):
- Day 0 (Wed): Gate open — internal canary 1% of traffic on region us-west1 for dedicated pilot customers only.
- Day 1 (Thu): Expand to 5% if no red flags. Begin lightweight customer outreach to pilot cohort.
- Day 3 (Sat): Decide to expand to 20% or rollback to 0% based on SLOs.
- Day 7 (following Tue): Post-mortem summary + decision on broader beta.

Rollout plan (ops checklist):
- Preflight (TODAY):
  - Feature flag created: advisor.autobatch.v1 (ops controls only).
  - Verify canary routing rule exists (policy: latency-first) — Rowan to confirm.
  - Add tracing tags: advisor.id, decision.reason, cache_hit (done).
  - Smoke tests: local + staging full runbook (Aisha).

- Day-of:
  - Flip 1% flag in infra; monitor first 30 minutes closely.
  - Standup: 30m after flip in #ops-autobatch (all on-call + product + dev).
  - Page on-call if p95 latency > baseline+40ms for >5m or error rate >0.5% absolute increase.

- Expansion criteria (manual gate):
  - No critical errors for 2h,
  - Latency thresholds met for 6h window,
  - Cost-signal trending positive or neutral,
  - No customer complaints in pilot cohort Slack thread.

- Rollback criteria (immediate):
  - Any customer-facing elevated 5xx spike (>0.3% absolute for >5m).
  - Sustained p95 degradation >40ms for >10m.
  - Regressions in model output quality tracked via eval buckets (drop >3% accuracy on smoke prompts).

Monitoring (metrics to watch):
- infra: p50/p95 latency, CPU/GPU util, queue length, request concurrency.
- advisor-specific: decisions/sec, cache_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, fallback_count.
- product: downstream token cost per request, success rates, and qualitative signal (open-ended).
- observability: traces with decision.reason for 100% of routed calls.

Slack comms (internal sample):
- Initial post (in #ops-autobatch and #prod-announce):
  "Starting 1% internal canary of Autobatch Advisor in us-west1. Flag: advisor.autobatch.v1. Monitoring window first 60m. Please escalate to @oncall if you see p95 latency > baseline + 40ms or new 5xx spikes. I'll post updates every 30m for the first 2 hours. — Brett"

- Customer note (pilot-only outreach template):
  "Hi <pilot-customer>, we just rolled a small optimization pilot behind the scenes (Autobatch Advisor) in your us-west1 traffic for improved request bundling. Expect unchanged responses; reach out if you see anything odd. — Product Ops"

Anticipated Q&A (prep):
- Q: Will responses change?
  A: No functional change expected. Advisor only adjusts batching/queueing heuristics; model outputs should be identical. We are tracking a smoke set of prompts to detect divergence.

- Q: What happens if latency increases?
  A: The advisor is behind a policy guardrail; if latency rises beyond thresholds we will auto-fallback to baseline routing and rollback flag. On-call will be paged per runbook.

- Q: Can we attribute cost impact quickly?
  A: Short-term delta will be noisy. Expect clearer signal after 24–72h for token-cost change on the mini cohort. We'll use per-route cost buckets in Optimize dashboard.

Escalation / contacts:
- On-call SRE: @oncall-sre (primary), fallback: Rowan Mitchell
- Product lead: Aisha Kapoor (optimize)
- Dev owner: Tomas Silva (autobatch runtime)
- Me (Brett) as comms owner — ping if you need me to open customer thread or escalate to support.

Edge cases & gotchas (notes to self):
- There is a known config quirk with the canary router where TTLs don't clear on rollback quickly — follow PR #748 steps for clean rollback.
- Ensure the cost reports aggregate by model+route otherwise we won't see the micro improvements.
- Watch for higher variance on low-volume customers — metrics can lie when n is small.

Post-launch follow-ups (if green):
- Collate 72h signal + quick notes, create a short 'pilot summary' doc and share with product-hosted-api and SRE (Rowan to lead).
- Prepare a short all-hands micro-update if we decide to widen beta (2–3 slides, 2 bullets).

TODOs (for next 48h):
- [ ] Rowan: confirm canary rule and rollback TTL behavior (deadline: today EOD).
- [ ] Aisha: run staging smoke tests with eval set and upload result to Confluence (deadline: tomorrow AM).
- [ ] Tomas: watch for fallback_count spikes and add an alert if >5 in 10m for canary.
- [ ] Brett: draft pilot summary template and send to opt-product slack channel after 72h.

Random scraps / brainstorm (keep here):
- Maybe add a micro-flag to force advisor to only try for requests > 128 tokens — reduces noise from small requests. Good for first week.
- Consider a user-visible opt-out later if customers prefer baseline behavior. Not in pilot.

End notes:
- This is mainly a personal working doc; will refine into a formal pilot playbook if initial run looks healthy.
- Keep comms short and frequent during roll.

Brett
